label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=7), plus last original token when L=9
explanation: A length/position unit that is active only around absolute steps 7-10 in long sequences. About 83% of activation mass sits on the <DEL> step: it fires on essentially every <DEL> when L=8 or 9 (precision ~1.0 for L>=8) and on roughly a third of <DEL> steps when L=7. It never fires on <DEL> for L<=6, or at any step t<=6. The other main source (~13% of mass) is the last original token (t=8) of L=9 sequences, where it fires about 80% of the time, more weakly than at <DEL>. Weak residual activity on the first copy step (recall_idx 1, input = first original token), mostly when L=9, accounts for the remaining ~3% of mass. Activation is roughly independent of token identity; the top activations are at <DEL> in L=8/9 sequences. It does not fire anywhere later in the copy phase (recall_idx>=2) or in short sequences.

issues: Factual error: the explanation says the unit fires on 'roughly a third' of <DEL> steps when L=7. Scoring (phase==1)&(L==7) gives precision 0.602 (dev), so it fires on about 60% of them. These activations are weak: 15.5% of active steps but only 7.1% of activation mass.

The other claims hold. <DEL> at L=8 has precision 0.999 and at L=9 precision 1.0. The L=9 last original token (orig_idx 8) has precision 0.807 and 13.2% of mass. recall_idx 1 holds about 3.4% of mass, mostly at L=9 (precision 0.28, versus 0.13 at L=8). Firing is essentially zero at t<=6 (2 steps), at L<=6 (4 steps) and at recall_idx>=2. The phase shares (83% / 13.5% / 3.4%) match.

No systematic gap on the test split. Misses (3.8% of mass) are the weak recall_idx 1 steps and rare L=9 orig_idx 7 steps (precision 0.027). False positives are mostly weak or zero L=7 <DEL> steps and some L=9 last-token steps. Splitting by token identity or digit count changes the L=7 <DEL> rate only modestly (0.54 to 0.75), so there is no clean extra condition.

Alternatives tried scored worse on dev F1: restricting to L>=8 gave 0.815, and adding L=9 recall_idx 1 gave 0.830. The original predicate (dev F1 0.864, reported test F1 0.863) looks close to the best available.
Not upheld only because of the misstated L=7 rate. The overall interpretation and the predicate are sound and should stand as explained once that number is corrected.
